{
  "claims": [
    {
      "anchor": "Redis offers three appendfsync policies",
      "claim_text": "Redis offers three appendfsync policies.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [
        {"sid": "P0.S0", "rel": "entails"},
        {"sid": "P0.S3", "rel": "entails"},
        {"sid": "P0.S5", "rel": "entails"}
      ],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage lists always, everysec, no."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "With appendfsync always, Redis calls fsync every time new commands are appended to the AOF",
      "claim_text": "With appendfsync always, Redis calls fsync every time new commands are appended to the AOF.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "which is very safe but very slow",
      "claim_text": "appendfsync always is very safe but very slow.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "The default policy is appendfsync no",
      "claim_text": "The default policy is appendfsync no.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [
        {"sid": "P1.S0", "rel": "refutes"},
        {"sid": "P2.S1", "rel": "refutes"}
      ],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passages say default is fsync every second."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "which leaves flushing to the operating system",
      "claim_text": "appendfsync no leaves flushing to the operating system.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S5", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "on Linux this normally means data is flushed every 30 seconds",
      "claim_text": "On Linux, appendfsync no normally means data is flushed every 30 seconds.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S7", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "With everysec you may lose about one second of data in a disaster",
      "claim_text": "With everysec you may lose about one second of data in a disaster.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [
        {"sid": "P0.S4", "rel": "entails"},
        {"sid": "P2.S2", "rel": "entails"}
      ],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Both passages state one second loss."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Because fsync runs on a background thread",
      "claim_text": "fsync runs on a background thread.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P2.S2", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "the main thread never has to wait for disk I/O",
      "claim_text": "The main thread never has to wait for disk I/O.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": false,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P2.S2", "rel": "refutes"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage says main thread tries hard to perform writes when no fsync is in progress, implying it may wait."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "appendfsync always typically cuts write throughput by more than half",
      "claim_text": "appendfsync always typically cuts write throughput by more than half.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": false,
      "evidence": [],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passages do not quantify throughput reduction."
    }
  ]
}
